source.author: cic
source.text: idque ita definimus; quod sit indifferens cum aestimatione mediocri; quod enim illi dicunt, id mihi ita occurrit, ut indifferens dicerem.
source.text_original: idque ita definimus; quod sit indifferens cum aestimatione mediocri; quod enim illi ἀδιάφορον dicunt, id mihi ita occurrit, ut indifferens dicerem.
source.text_english: And this is how we define it: that which is indifferent with moderate value; for what they say, that occurred to me in such a way that I should call it indifferent.

reuse.author: hier
reuse.text: callidissimus aduersarius et inueteratus dierum malorum nouit alia esse, quae extrinsecus sint et a philosophis quoque mundi , hoc est indifferentia, nominentur, in eorumque amissione atque contemptu perfectam non esse uirtutem, alia, quae intrinsecus et de se data cogunt dolere perdentem.
reuse.text_original: callidissimus aduersarius et inueteratus dierum malorum nouit alia esse, quae extrinsecus sint et a philosophis quoque mundi ἀδιάφορα, hoc est indifferentia, nominentur, in eorumque amissione atque contemptu perfectam non esse uirtutem, alia, quae intrinsecus et de se data cogunt dolere perdentem.
reuse.text_english: The most cunning and long-standing enemy of evil days knows that there are other things, which are external and are called by philosophers of the world as well, that is, indifferent things, and that in the loss and contempt of these virtue is not complete; and there are other things, which are inward and, as given by themselves, compel one to grieve when they are lost.
